title: DL560 TermAl host process restarted at 06:43:39Z with no known operator action, killing a running test run
outcome: Reported by Opus2 (#7535) from C7's read-only facts (#3604/#3605), 2026-11-22. The w-b3c1 GREEN7 run test-9b5bc520 on DL560 C7 died at about 06:43:35Z (SIGKILL, cleanup trigger "launcher-exit", mid-compile). DL560's TermAl host process (target/release/termal, pid 2918479) STARTED at 06:43:39Z, 5 s after the run's last log write. C7's codex app-server restarted at 06:46:11Z. The OS was not rebooted (uptime since Nov 9), and journalctl -k has no OOM lines. Central's federation status at about 06:43Z showed DL560's host utilization briefly as unavailable/peerDisconnected/stale (the last snapshot 06:43:09Z), then fresh at 06:43:19Z, while the link record stayed at worker attempt 2. No deliberate restart by Greg is known to the coordinator. The cause is not assumed: a crash, an external restart, or a host-side lifecycle action.
acceptance: The reason the DL560 TermAl host process ended before 06:43:39Z is identified from DL560's own records (host lifecycle journal, previousInstance from GET /api/diagnostics/host-lifecycle, console log), read through supported routes, never SSH, or recorded as unknown with what was checked.

If a TermAl defect caused it: a behaviour test that fails before the fix, the fix in the owning mechanism, a clean review pair and the full gate. If it was an operator or environment action: a recorded disposition.
